newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spain's debt closed lower on Monday after a French request to put off final approval of the budget stability pact increased worries of EMU's delays, taking a toll on peripheral government markets, dealers said.
But bonos limited losses as domestic buying emerged on dip.
"We outperformed Italian bonds, but we've also tracked down with them, with the spread (over Bunds) widening," said Francisco Castanera, dealer at BNP in Madrid.
The 10-year spread over Bunds was trading at around 87 bps before the close, after a low at 89 basis points. It started this morning at around 81 basis points.

"The long-term bond future is likely to stay above a level of around 114.50/114.80," said Emilio Sainz, dealer at Natwest in Madrid, "and the (10-year) spread will not widen to more than 90 or 95 basis points," he added.
Dealers said solid economic background was offering bonos very good support, and they ruled out that the French request could jeopardise the EMU project.

"Spanish May CPI will come out very good on Friday," a dealer said. But despite expectations for a yearly rate down to 1.5 percent versus 1.7 percent in April, dealers were ruling out a fresh rate cut before the Amsterdam's summit next week.
